title: CIA's psychic spy saw an ancient city on Mars before its apocalypse
excerpt: The CIA's most gifted remote viewer once saw a thriving city on the Martian surface. Now, more people have seen the horrific end of the Red Planet and are sharing the details.
content:
In May 1984, a CIA psychic spy claimed he traveled through space and time to see the end of a thriving civilization on Mars. Now, more people who claim they have seen the same vision are sharing the horrific ending of the Martian race.

A man who identified himself only as 'Brady' told the Daily Mail he possessed the ability to practice astral projection - where your awareness leaves your physical body and travels elsewhere while you remain connected to it.

Using this technique, Brady claimed he found himself in a terrifying vision on Mars, but a Mars that was inhabited by alien creatures in the distant past.

The man claimed the experience was 'heartbreaking and drastic' as an apocalyptic blue wave wiped out the Martian civilization.

Brady said: 'Everyone suddenly panicked, most looked up, others ran. There were screams and panic echoing off the side of buildings, I stared up and pierced my eyes through the bright daylight and there was a celestial body hurling towards the planet.'

'It was circular in shape, profoundly large, I felt a sigh of desperation and acceptance of fate,' he continued.

At this point, Brady claimed he watched in horror as the ground shook and a giant wave emerged from the horizon, swallowing up everything in its path.

Brady and others over the years have claimed they saw this destruction on Mars, describing the apocalypse with almost the exact same details as CIA remote reviewer Joe McMoneagle - who was tasked with seeing life on Mars one million years ago.

Remote viewers and others with psychic visions have claimed that a thriving civilization once lived on Mars (Stock Image)

In the 1970s and 1980s, the CIA carried out repeated experiments with individuals who had allegedly been trained to perceive information about distant places, locations or people - calling these operatives 'remote viewers.'

The Cold War effort mainly targeted Russia's Soviet Union, and McMoneagle has widely been regarded as the agency's best remote viewer, using his ability to see inside top-secret facilities - like a Soviet hangar building a new type of submarine in 1979.

During the 1984 experiment, which was part of the CIA's Project Stargate, the secretive US military program to weaponize remote viewing abilities, McMoneagle was handed a paper card with a new target printed on it.

This time, his target to psychically visit was: 'The planet Mars. Time of interest, approximately one million years BC.'

McMoneagle has said in interviews since the operation that he was not told what he would be looking at, adding that his visions of a civilized Mars came spontaneously.

Guided by coordinates on the Martian surface given to him by intelligence officials, McMoneagle 'visited' the Cydonia Mensae region - the location of the 'Face on Mars' photo taken by the Viking orbiter.

McMoneagle told his supervisor in a now-declassified report: 'I kind of got an oblique view of a pyramid or pyramid form. It's very high. It's kind of sitting in a large, depressed area. It's yellowish, okra colored.'

Instructed to 'move in time,' McMoneagle then encountered visions of what seemed to be a dying alien race on the Red Planet.

Pictured: Joe McMoneagle, a former CIA remote viewer during the Cold War

McMoneagle added in his remote viewing transcript: 'I'm seeing... it's like a perception of a shadow of people, very tall... thin. It's only a shadow. It's as if they were there and they're not, not there anymore.'

The psychic spy described pyramid structures, carved canyons and obelisks, dust storms and atmospheric breakdown - suggesting that the inhabitants of Mars may have been ready to move to another world.

In the decades since McMoneagle’s vision, others have claimed they visited the planet, with Brady describing how he 'chased the experience' by attempting to project his consciousness over and over again onto the Red Planet.

He told the Daily Mail that addiction reached a point where all he cared about was returning to his vision of Mars.

Brady described the city that was destroyed as looking similar to Dubai. 'However, the atmosphere and environment seemed to look like England on a summer's day,' he added.

'Where I was it was bustling, vibrant and active with people everywhere. Everyone was around six to seven feet tall, really slim, with pale white blueish skin tone.'

The unusual stone mesas of the Cydonia region on Mars where McMoneagle allegedly visited in a remote viewing session in 1984

Brady is not the only person who claimed to have visited something resembling McMoneagle’s Mars remote vision.

Remote viewer Courtney Brown described his own visions of Mars in two books, Cosmic Voyage and Cosmic Explorers.

Brown, an associate professor of political science at Emory University, claimed to have conducted large-scale experiments with multiple remote viewers examining the surface of Mars.

Brown said he 'visited' the Cydonia region McMoneagle visited and saw a civilization of ancient Martians with prominent eyes and delicate bone structure.

Like McMoneagle, he claimed that the Martian civilization was subjected to a catastrophic event, but suggested that survivors may have found homes elsewhere in the solar system.

Brown wrote: 'At its peak, Martian society compared technologically to that of ancient Egypt. They were people who lived under harsh conditions. But they could feed their families, live in towns and participate in community life. Martian society experienced some major catastrophe. Many Martians died.'

McMoneagle’s strange vision has attracted attention for decades in part because some of his other remote viewing experiments were so accurate.

The 1979 incident with the Soviet submarine is among his most famous sessions, as McMoneagle claimed to have 'seen' a large warehouse 100 yards from the White Sea in northern Russia.

He described a never-before-seen type of submarine with slanted missile tubes and a unique double-hull structure.

His claims were dismissed by the intelligence community, but defense officials later confirmed the Soviet Union was building a new class of submarine, the Typhoon, which was unveiled in 1980.
